description:
Advances: specled.package

Review-bar-override: a gate proposal, not a defect — the class has now appeared in three review arcs and should stop being reportable.

From the critical review of specled_-n5q (Recurring class 1).

Comment prose duplicating ADR prose keeps recurring (F11 here; the same class appeared in the s65 and 0y8 arcs). It is not merely verbose — it goes FALSE independently of the ADR. This ticket own commit log records two restatements that had already drifted from the ADR they restated and needed a remediation commit.

Two options, cheapest first:
1. A rule that comment blocks longer than ~8 lines in lib/specled_ex/realization/ must end in a specled.decision.* pointer. Mechanical, no false positives worth worrying about.
2. Richer: flag a lib comment block over N lines containing a sentence that also appears in a .spec/decisions/ file. Catches the duplication at write time rather than the missing pointer.

Start with 1.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.decisions

(SUBJECT ASSIGNMENT DECIDED BY THE OPERATOR. The ticket said specled.package; that is wrong.
specled.package is the distributed-artifact subject — README, docs, skills, mix.exs,
lib/specled_ex.ex. A lint over lib/specled_ex/realization/ comment hygiene is repo-internal
policy, not package surface, and the choice is permanent. Frame the new requirement as
ADR-REFERENCE DISCIPLINE under .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md, subject id
specled.decisions — that is what the rule actually is: it exists to stop comment prose from
drifting away from the ADR it restates.)

BLOCKED BY specled_-vzd.4, and the ordering matters for more than merge mechanics. vzd.4 item 4
trims exactly the blocks this lint would flag. api_boundary.ex:164-184 and
orchestrator.ex:478-490 are SIMULTANEOUSLY two of the blocks vzd.4 deletes and two of the ten
this lint would demand a pointer on. If this ticket landed first, a worker would bolt an ADR
pointer onto 21 lines of prose vzd.4 then deletes 17 of — wasted work that also perversely
SATISFIES the lint while leaving the duplicated-ADR-prose defect in place, the exact failure
mode this ticket exists to prevent. After vzd.4, your remediation surface drops from 10 blocks
to 8.

MEASUREMENT YOU NEED — the naive rule fails on 10 of 11 blocks. Sweeping
lib/specled_ex/realization/*.ex for contiguous `#` blocks >= 8 lines at the epic base gives 11,
and EXACTLY ONE already ends in a specled.decision.* pointer:
  api_boundary.ex:164-184    (21)  ends "...which is recoverable."          NO POINTER
  implementation.ex:111-124  (14)  ends specled.decision.realized_by_tier_implication   OK
  implementation.ex:467-480  (14)                                           NO POINTER
  orchestrator.ex:161-168     (8)  section banner (# ----)                  NO POINTER
  orchestrator.ex:191-203    (13)                                           NO POINTER
  orchestrator.ex:216-248    (33)  numbered two-phase algorithm walkthrough NO POINTER
  orchestrator.ex:366-374     (9)                                           NO POINTER
  orchestrator.ex:478-490    (13)                                           NO POINTER
  orchestrator.ex:717-735    (19)                                           NO POINTER
  orchestrator.ex:809-822    (14)  ends "See atlas-vmi." (not an ADR id)    NO POINTER
  orchestrator.ex:955-964    (10)                                           NO POINTER

CARVE-OUT IS MANDATORY, DESIGN IT BEFORE WRITING THE RULE. Two blocks CANNOT honestly carry an
ADR pointer: orchestrator.ex:161-168 is a `# ----` section banner, and orchestrator.ex:216-248
is a numbered algorithm walkthrough that restates no ADR. The lint therefore needs a stated
carve-out — banner blocks, and/or an explicit opt-out marker mirroring the existing
spec-lint:allow-code= discipline (test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:165-183). Pin the
carve-out's scope in the must the way specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity pins its marker
to .spec/decisions/ only.

DECISION-CLASS: code + spec amendment. Draft fully and record completion normally; the
orchestrator will NOT merge without human sign-off.

Allowed touches:
- test/realization_comment_pointer_lint_test.exs  (new)
- .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md
- lib/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary.ex, orchestrator.ex, implementation.ex
  (remediation pointers only)
- .spec/specs/api_boundary.spec.md, .spec/specs/branch_guard.spec.md,
  .spec/specs/implementation_tier.spec.md  (surface owners of the files you add pointers to)
A new file under test/ belongs to no subject surface (same status as
test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs today), so it emits branch_guard_unmapped_change at WARNING,
not pinned to error in .spec/config.yml. Non-blocking.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/specled_ex/ outside realization/
- docs/**
- .spec/decisions/**  (do not rewrite the ADRs themselves)
- .spec/specs/package.spec.md  (the subject was moved off package deliberately)

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT implement option 2 (sentence-overlap against .spec/decisions/). The ticket says start
  with option 1.
- Do not widen beyond lib/specled_ex/realization/.
- Do not rewrite the ADRs themselves.
- Do not "while I'm here" fix orchestrator.ex:809-822's bare "See atlas-vmi." pointer beyond
  what your own rule requires of it.

Verification:
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix test test/realization_comment_pointer_lint_test.exs
  mix test --only spec:<your new requirement id>
  mix format --check-formatted
  make xref
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
Stub flip: NONE required IF your new requirement joins decision_governance.spec.md's existing
execute: true tagged_tests block. Verify that block exists before assuming it does.

Expected diff: 6-8 files, ~220 lines.

Mechanical checks:

Semantic checks:
- Lint bites on the LIVE corpus: YES, proven. corpus_files/0 uses Path.wildcard over the real tree (12 files; guard asserts >= 10). On a scratch copy outside the repo (/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/vzd6copy) I appended an 8-line unpointed comment block to lib/specled_ex/realization/drift.ex; the lint went RED naming it: "lib/specled_ex/realization/drift.ex:137-144 (8 lines) has no terminal specled.decision.* pointer". Restored; scratch and stage worktrees both report empty git status --porcelain.
- Shipped tree green: YES. mix test test/realization_comment_pointer_lint_test.exs -> 9 tests, 0 failures. Independent awk sweep of the current tree finds exactly 8 blocks >= 8 lines, all accounted for: implementation.ex:111-124 (pre-existing pointer), implementation.ex:467-481 (new pointer), orchestrator.ex:165-172 (banner), 195-209 (new pointer), 231-264 (marker), 382-391 (marker), 724-743 (new pointer), 784-798 (new pointer).
- Exemption is narrow, not an escape hatch: MOSTLY, with one real hole. All by execution against the live corpus:
  * empty reason (spec-lint:allow-long-comment=) -> REJECTED, block still flagged.
  * non-terminal marker (marker on line 8 of 9, prose after) -> REJECTED.
  * ADR id mid-block but not terminal -> REJECTED.

Harmless, but the test's claim describes a helper-level property, not a live one.

I appended 12 lines of ordinary architectural prose wrapped in two hyphen rules to a real realization file and the lint stayed GREEN. Wrapping any block in "# ---" silences it, with no reason required - a cheaper and less visible opt-out than the marker the spec designed. Bounded by shape, but the shape swallows arbitrary prose.
- Threshold: 8 enforced, 7 ignored: CONFIRMED by execution on the live corpus. 7-line appended prose block -> 0 failures; the same block at 8 lines -> flagged as "(8 lines)". No off-by-one.
- Every added pointer/marker is TRUE: NO - two of six are wrong. Followed all four ADRs.

ADR Decision 2 ("Prune split") states read-time filtering is authoritative and that a nil/empty manifest never filters, exactly what the block says. (Redundant: the block already cited the same ADR mid-prose at line 472; the added line is pure lint tax.)
  * orchestrator.ex:195-209 -> specled.decision.divergence_refresh_scope: TRUE. ADR Decision + third Consequence state the {tier, mfa}-scoped exclusion and the drift+divergence run-wide withholding verbatim; the code gate at 210-213 matches.
  * orchestrator.ex:784-798 -> specled.decision.silent_seed_batches_subject_graph: TRUE, and a genuine improvement over the bare "See atlas-vmi." it replaces. ADR Decision 1 matches the block clause for clause, including the subject:B:hash:unknown failure mode.
  * orchestrator.ex:724-743 -> specled.decision.realized_by_tier_implication: GAP 1 (below).
  * orchestrator.ex:231-264 marker "implementation algorithm walkthrough; no governing ADR": GAP 2 (below).
  * orchestrator.ex:382-391 marker "implementation data-shape walkthrough; no governing ADR": defensible. The block describes a private helper's triple shape and ordering determinism; no ADR specifies that.
- No double-remediation of blocks vzd.4 already fixed: CONFIRMED. api_boundary.ex is absent from the diff and now carries no block >= 8 lines. The old orchestrator.ex:478-490 region is gone (vzd.4). The orchestrator diff is five pointer/marker insertions plus one rewrap of the "See atlas-vmi." line; no deletions, no re-trimming.
- Targeted verification: mix test test/realization_comment_pointer_lint_test.exs -> 9 tests, 0 failures. mix test --only spec:specled.decisions.adr_reference_discipline -> 1348 tests, 0 failures, 1342 excluded. mix format --check-formatted -> exit 0. make xref -> clean at --fail-above 0 (MIX_ENV=test). mix spec.check --no-run-commands -> validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0; spec.check result=pass.
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:
- GAP 1 - the pointer at orchestrator.ex:743 certifies a block whose final substantive sentence is FALSE. Lines 741-742 read "The post-run refresh_and_commit_hashes/4 is unaffected; it still runs under the same gate when no drift is detected and uses write/2's replacement semantics for the full realization map." The function at orchestrator.ex:873-897 calls HashStore.merge(root, realization), and its own first comment line (874) says "Flat-tier refresh only. MUST merge, not replace: HashStore.write/2 would wipe the implementation ... section that silent-seed just wrote." specled.decision.silent_seed_batches_subject_graph Decision 2 makes the same statement ("refresh_and_commit_hashes/3 uses HashStore.merge/2, not write/2"). The named ADR (realized_by_tier_implication, Decision 5) accurately covers the silent-seed pass but says nothing about the refresh side, so the pointer does not cover the false clause - and the ADR that does cover it is the one cited 45 lines further down, saying the opposite. The falsehood is pre-existing (base 722494b5, and it also appears in the @moduledoc at line 26 and the @doc at line 101, both out of this lint's scope), but this ticket exists to stop exactly this class and the remediation stamped an ADR pointer on it instead of correcting it. Fix: correct the sentence to merge/2 semantics (and ideally point the block at silent_seed_batches_subject_graph, or at both).
- GAP 2 - the marker reason at orchestrator.ex:264 asserts "no governing ADR" for build_attestations/4, and that is false. specled.decision.file_touch_yields_to_realization governs this function directly, and the 34-line block restates its Decision section nearly clause for clause: block step 1 = ADR condition 2 (binding not in this run's realization_drift/dangling findings); step 2 = ADR condition 1 plus its "resolver returns nil / hot-reloaded module" consequence; step 3 = ADR condition 1's "after Path.relative_to/2 normalization"; step 4 = the ADR's :attested_clean per-(file, subject) predicate; Phase 2 = the ADR's "tagged-tests targets covering attested requirements expand to the corresponding test files (looked up via index["test_tags"][rid])". This is the single largest ADR-restating comment in the corpus, and it is now stamped with an exemption that positively claims no ADR governs it - the exact defect the ticket was opened to eliminate, converted from "missing pointer" into "asserted absence". The ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT's own framing ("restates no ADR") was the source of the error, so this is a contract measurement being wrong rather than an implementer inventing a claim; but the marker text ships as a false statement. Fix: replace the marker with a terminal specled.decision.file_touch_yields_to_realization pointer (the block then needs no exemption at all), or trim the ADR-restating clauses and keep only the implementation-specific mechanics under an honest reason.

Notes (advisory only):
- The banner carve-out (see above) is the weakest link in the design. Tightening it to require the interior to be short and free of sentence-shaped prose, or requiring the banner's interior line count to be under the threshold, would close it without touching the marker discipline.
- The lint validates pointer SHAPE only, never existence. I appended a block ending in "See `specled.decision.this_adr_does_not_exist`." to a real realization file and the lint stayed GREEN. Since the ticket's premise is that pointers go stale, cross-checking the id against the .spec/decisions/ filenames is a two-line addition (Path.wildcard on .spec/decisions/*.md) with real value. Not required by the contract's option 1, so advisory.
- assert length(files) >= 10 against 12 actual files leaves only two files of slack before the no-op guard stops guarding. Consider pinning the exact count or raising the floor.
- The implementation.ex:481 pointer duplicates a reference already present at line 472. Expect more of this: for blocks that already cite an ADR mid-prose the rule adds a line of pure ceremony. Allowing a pointer anywhere in the block's LAST paragraph rather than strictly the last line would remove that tax without weakening the rule (the non-terminal rejection test would need rewording).

ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION — Gap 2 originates in a factual claim I made without checking. Read before
grading the implementer.

My contract asserted, as measurement:

  "orchestrator.ex:216-248 is a numbered algorithm walkthrough that restates no ADR"

and listed it as one of two blocks that "CANNOT honestly carry an ADR pointer". The implementer
built its exemption marker on that assertion and wrote the reason "implementation algorithm
walkthrough; no governing ADR".

THE ASSERTION IS FALSE. specled.decision.file_touch_yields_to_realization governs build_attestations/4
directly, and the verifier traced the block restating that ADR's Decision section nearly clause for
clause — step 1 = ADR condition 2, step 2 = condition 1 plus its resolver-nil consequence, step 3 =
condition 1's Path.relative_to normalization, step 4 = the :attested_clean per-(file, subject)
predicate, Phase 2 = the tagged-tests expansion. It is the single largest ADR-restating comment in
the corpus.

So the remediation converted the defect from "missing pointer" into "ASSERTED ABSENCE" — a marker
that positively claims no ADR governs a block that is a near-transcription of one. That is worse
than the original state and it is precisely the class this ticket was opened to eliminate. The
marker text ships as a false statement because I supplied a false premise.

THIS IS THE SECOND TIME IN THIS EPIC that a factual claim in a contract I wrote turned out to be
wrong, and both had the same cause: I copied an analyst's measurement into an authoritative-sounding
contract line without verifying it. The first was the arming.ex "precedent" on specled_-dn4.12
(arming.ex IS on a surface list; I said it was not). Both were caught by cold verification, which is
the system working — but the contract is supposed to be the thing workers can trust, and twice it
was not. Pattern recorded on the epic.

CONTRACT AMENDED: the claim that the :216-264 block restates no ADR is WITHDRAWN. The carve-out is
still needed for the genuine banner case, but this block is not an instance of it.

WHAT IS NOT MINE:
- Gap 1 is the implementer's. The pointer added at orchestrator.ex:743 certifies a block whose final
  sentence is FALSE — it claims refresh_and_commit_hashes/4 "uses write/2's replacement semantics"
  when the function calls HashStore.merge and its own comment at :874 says "MUST merge, not replace".
  The falsehood is pre-existing, but stamping an ADR pointer onto a false paragraph is exactly what
  this lint exists to prevent, and the named ADR does not even cover that clause.
- The banner exemption being too broad is a design choice the contract did not dictate.
  section_banner?/1 checks only that the first and last comment lines are hyphen rules; the middle is
  unconstrained, so wrapping 12 lines of ordinary prose in "# ---" silences the lint with NO reason
  required — a cheaper and less visible opt-out than the marker the spec deliberately designed.

Routing to a cold auditor. Auditor: grade Gap 1 and the banner hole as the implementer's; treat
Gap 2's PREMISE as mine and judge only whether the implementer should have caught that its marker
reason was false before writing it.

AUDIT: BOUNCE → implementer
Session: 9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f.jsonl

Independent audit. All probes run against a copy of the real 12-file realization corpus
(scratchpad/vzd6audit) with the test module's helpers extracted verbatim; stage worktree
untouched (git status --porcelain empty, HEAD 87ca894a). mix test
test/realization_comment_pointer_lint_test.exs -> 9 tests, 0 failures.

Gap 1 (false-certified pointer): REAL, and the implementer's. Upheld, with evidence the
verifier did not surface.
- The clause: orchestrator.ex:739-742 "The post-run refresh_and_commit_hashes/4 ... uses
  write/2's replacement semantics for the full realization map." The function
  (orchestrator.ex:873-899) calls HashStore.merge(root, realization) and computes over
  @flat_tiers only. The sentence is false TWICE: merge, not write; flat tiers, not the full
  map. Its own header at :874 says "MUST merge, not replace: HashStore.write/2 would wipe
  the implementation ... section that silent-seed just wrote."
- The named ADR does not cover it and contradicts it. realized_by_tier_implication Decision 5
  says the SEED persists "via ... HashStore.merge/2 (additive deep-merge, in contrast to
  write/2's replacement semantics)"; Decision 2 says the refresh side is "unobservable
  through run/2 under merge/2 semantics". silent_seed_batches_subject_graph — cited 45 lines
  below at :798 — Decision 2 is titled exactly "refresh_and_commit_hashes/3 uses
  HashStore.merge/2, not write/2", and its Context section records the write/2 baseline-wipe
  as a fixed defect.
- NEW: the false clause is a mis-transcription of the very ADR the pointer names. The comment
  took Decision 5's parenthetical "in contrast to write/2's replacement semantics", dropped
  the contrast, and reattached write/2 to the refresh. This is not merely "a false sentence
  that happened to get a pointer" — it is a textbook instance of the exact drift class the
  ticket was opened to eliminate, and the pointer certifies the drifted copy against its own
  source. That makes stamping it this ticket's defect regardless of the falsehood being
  pre-existing at base (confirmed pre-existing: 722494b5 orchestrator.ex:739).
- Implementer culpability: it had to open realized_by_tier_implication to write the pointer,
  and Decision 5 is the correcting sentence. Mitigation noted: the contract's "remediation
  pointers only" wording arguably fences prose edits — but the honest response to that fence
  is to escalate, not to certify. Bounce stands.
- Fix: correct the clause to merge/2 + flat-tier scope, and point the block at
  silent_seed_batches_subject_graph (or name both ADRs, with the decision id terminal).

Gap 2 (marker asserting "no governing ADR"): premise is the orchestrator's; the implementer
should still have caught it. Verdict: YES, diligence failure — secondary to Gap 1, not the
routing reason.
- Reason: the marker is a positive factual assertion shipped in product comment text, under a
  ticket whose entire premise is that such assertions go false. Whoever writes the sentence
  owns verifying it; a contract premise is a hypothesis to measure, not a warrant to ship.
- The check was one hop and local. The block's own header at :193-194 reads
  "# covers: specled.realized_by.orchestrator_publishes_attestations";
  .spec/specs/realized_by.spec.md:43 lists specled.decision.file_touch_yields_to_realization
  in that subject's decisions:. The implementer had to read the block end to end to place a
  terminal marker on it.
- I re-traced the restatement independently and confirm the verifier's mapping is exact
  (block steps 1-4 and Phase 2 against the ADR's four-condition Decision + tagged-tests
  expansion clause). It is the largest ADR restatement in the corpus.
- Credit where due: the implementer did NOT blanket-apply the claim. The second marker at
  :391 makes the identical "no governing ADR" assertion and it is TRUE (see spot-check).
- NEW design point, cheap and durable: a marker reason that asserts ADR NON-existence is
  itself a stale-able claim — the failure mode the lint exists to catch, rebuilt inside the
  escape hatch. Marker reasons should state what the block IS ("private helper data-shape
  walkthrough"), never what does not exist. Drop "no governing ADR" from both markers.

Banner exemption hole: REPRODUCED, and blocking.
- Probe: 12 lines of ordinary architectural prose wrapped in two hyphen rules, appended to
  the real drift.ex -> lint GREEN. Controls on the same corpus: 8 plain lines -> RED
  ("drift.ex:137-144 (8 lines)"); 7 plain lines -> GREEN; unmodified corpus -> GREEN.
  section_banner?/1 inspects List.first and List.last only.
- Severity: design flaw, not an acceptable shape carve-out. It is a no-reason,
  review-invisible opt-out that is STRICTLY cheaper than the designed marker, and cost
  asymmetry decides adoption: the marker forces a reason a reviewer sees in the diff, "# ---"
  reads as formatting. It voids the lint for precisely the class most at risk — long
  architectural prose. Note also that the live corpus's only banner (orchestrator.ex:165-172)
  already has a 6-line prose interior explaining do_run/2's design, i.e. the carve-out is
  already carrying prose today.
- Recommended fix — do NOT add a second constraint on top of the shape test. DELETE the
  banner exemption and stop counting hyphen-rule separator lines toward block length. A real
  divider is 1-3 lines and never reaches 8; orchestrator.ex:165-172 stays green by SIZE
  (6 interior < 8) rather than by shape; my 12-line probe goes red. That removes a carve-out
  from the design instead of hardening one, keeps the corpus honest, and simplifies the
  must-statement (which currently names the banner carve-out and must be reworded).
  Interior caps and "no sentence-shaped prose" heuristics both fail: the first flags the
  repo's own banner, the second is unspecifiable.

Spot-check of the four the verifier certified TRUE — all four confirmed, one caveat:
- implementation.ex:467-481 -> tracer_manifest_merge_on_flush: TRUE. ADR Decision 2 "Prune
  split" states read-time filtering is authoritative, seed-time prune merely bounds file
  growth, and "a nil or empty manifest never filters" — the block's three claims, in order.
  Redundancy confirmed (same ADR already cited at :471-472).
- orchestrator.ex:195-209 -> divergence_refresh_scope: TRUE. ADR Decision (exclusion is
  {tier, mfa}, store has no subject dimension) and Consequence 3 (drift+divergence under
  --accept-drift withhold together) match; the gate at :210-213 matches both. CAVEAT: this
  block is two-topic — its first half (drift/dangling gating) is covered only by the
  mid-block requirement reference specled.realized_by.drift_acceptance, not by the terminal
  ADR. True as written, but it is the same structure that produced Gap 1: one terminal
  pointer certifying a block whose uncovered half is where a falsehood can hide.
- orchestrator.ex:784-798 -> silent_seed_batches_subject_graph: TRUE, clause for clause
  against ADR Decision 1 including the subject:B:hash:unknown mechanism. Real improvement
  over "See atlas-vmi."
- orchestrator.ex:382-391 marker "implementation data-shape walkthrough; no governing ADR":
  claim VERIFIED, not merely defensible. Searched .spec/decisions/ for impl_bindings /
  requirement provenance / subject-then-requirement / aggregation: no hit. The nearest
  candidate, deterministic_hashing, scopes to term_to_binary serialization only, not
  attestation list ordering. No ADR governs all_subject_requirement_mfa_triples/1.
Also re-confirmed independently: no double-remediation of vzd.4 (diff touches only
implementation.ex and orchestrator.ex; api_boundary.ex absent), threshold 8/7 exact on the
live corpus, and the new requirement joins an existing execute: true tagged_tests block
(decision_governance.spec.md:173-186) so no stub flip was owed.

Advisory promotions:
- Pointer EXISTENCE check: PROMOTE TO BLOCKING. Reproduced GREEN on a block ending
  "See `specled.decision.this_adr_does_not_exist`." A nonexistent pointer is materially WORSE
  than no pointer, not equivalent: it satisfies the lint and thereby suppresses the very
  demand that would produce a real one, while reading to a human as certification. The
  decisive argument is internal consistency — the requirement now lives under
  specled.decisions, whose existing must specled.decisions.reference_validation
  (decision_governance.spec.md:43-55) already requires warning "when a subject references an
  unknown ADR id". Shipping a sibling requirement in the same file that accepts unknown ADR
  ids in code comments is a self-contradiction in one subject. Cost is ~3 lines
  (Path.wildcard(".spec/decisions/*.md") -> MapSet of ids). Orchestrator must amend the
  contract to authorize it — it is beyond option 1 as written.
- Corpus floor: NON-BLOCKING, fold in while the file is open. assert length(files) >= 10
  against 12 real files. Pin to == 12 with a message naming the expected count, or raise to
  >= 12.
- Terminal-only rule: KEEP AS IS, no change. "Last paragraph" needs a paragraph definition
  ("#"-only separator lines) and introduces a fresh ambiguity class to save one line on the
  two blocks that already cite mid-prose. More importantly, terminal position is what makes
  the pointer certify the WHOLE block; a "somewhere near the end is fine" rule is the
  partial-coverage reading that Gap 1 is an instance of. The implementation.ex:481 duplicate
  is acceptable ceremony.

Bounce reason — implementer must fix, in this order:
1. Correct orchestrator.ex:741-742 to HashStore.merge/2 semantics over the flat tiers only,
   and repoint the block (silent_seed_batches_subject_graph terminal, or both ADRs with a
   decision id last).
2. Replace the orchestrator.ex:264 marker with a terminal
   specled.decision.file_touch_yields_to_realization pointer — the block then needs no
   exemption at all.
3. Close the banner hole by deleting section_banner?/1 and excluding hyphen-rule separator
   lines from the length count; reword the must-statement's banner clause to match; replace
   the "a bounded section banner is exempt" test with one asserting a prose-interior banner
   is REJECTED and the live 6-interior-line banner is accepted by size.
4. Add the ADR-id existence check against .spec/decisions/*.md plus a rejection test — ONLY
   after the orchestrator amends the contract (item below).
5. Reword both marker reasons to state what the block is; delete "no governing ADR".
6. Raise or pin the corpus floor.
Must NOT be touched: the lint mechanism and block-chunking approach; the 8-line threshold;
the marker discipline (terminal, reason-bearing, non-empty, corpus-scoped) and its four
rejection-path tests; the three TRUE pointers at implementation.ex:481,
orchestrator.ex:209, orchestrator.ex:798; the :391 marker's substance (reword only);
api_boundary.ex (vzd.4's surface); .spec/decisions/** ; package.spec.md.
Out of scope, file a descope ticket instead: the SAME write/2 falsehood appears at
orchestrator.ex:27 (@moduledoc) and :101 (@doc). Both are doc attributes, not "#" blocks, so
this lint cannot see them and the ticket's surface does not include them. Three sites total
is evidence the class is real, not an argument to widen this ticket.

Orchestrator contract correction required:
1. WITHDRAW (already done in the correction comment) the "orchestrator.ex:216-248 restates no
   ADR" measurement and, with it, the claim that TWO blocks cannot honestly carry a pointer.
   Only the banner case ever qualified — and under the recommended fix even that stops being
   a carve-out.
2. Tighten "remediation pointers only" in Allowed touches. As written it fences the
   implementer out of correcting false prose in the very blocks it is stamping, which is the
   ambiguity Gap 1 hid behind. Replace with: "pointers, markers, and correction of any clause
   the pointer would certify".
3. Authorize the ADR-id existence check explicitly (it exceeds option 1 as the ticket framed
   it) and state that option 2 remains out of scope.
4. Note in the epic pattern record that both contract errors so far were unverified
   measurements copied into authoritative-sounding contract lines; the durable fix is a rule
   that contract measurements about ADR coverage must cite the grep that produced them.

Mechanical-remedy bounce count this ticket: 0/2. First bounce on vzd.6, and I do not score it
mechanical — every item requires judgment about ADR coverage, not a rote re-run.

title: Lint: long comment blocks in lib/realization must end in an ADR pointer, not restate the ADR
